text:
sam: Starting bring-up for nyc-gpu-cluster-02, hitting a hard stop during nodegroup bootstrap. Need eyes.

maya: saw one failed ASG launch, attaching logs. Could be subnet tagging.

leo: what error are you seeing? short snippet helps.

sam: deploy-bot reported: `ERROR: instance launch failed: subnet has no 'redwood:nodepool' tag`

deploy-bot: Automated deploy status: FAILED at step=cloud-provision, code=SubnetTagMissing, details='Missing tag redwood:nodepool on subnet subnet-0a1b2c3d'

maya: ah that explains it. The terraform module expects `tags = { "redwood:nodepool" = var.nodepool }` but our bootstrap script omitted it for the new NYC VPC.

sam: ugh, that was my terraform change. I mistakenly used `tag` instead of `tags`. I'll patch and re-run plan.

leo: also saw kubelet flapping on the partially created nodes after the failed launches: `failed to register node: unable to verify node ip` — might be egress/NAT issue in the new subnet routing.

sam: stack trace from join attempt pasted: ```
Jun 24 14:12:03 kubelet[1234]: E0624 14:12:03.123456    1234 kubelet.go:2171] Failed to register node: error getting node address: interface eth0: no route to host
```

maya: that matches the VPC route table — the NAT gateway wasn't attached to the private subnet. The ops playbook step to attach nat-01 for nyc was skipped by the provisioning runner.

infra-ops: tagging + NAT fix needed. Suggest rollback the partial ASG to avoid stray on-demand instances and extra billing.

sam: starting rollback of module nyc-asg via terraform: `terraform destroy -target=module.asg -auto-approve`

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by sam. Step=destroy, target=module.asg.

leo: quick note — the spot pool was configured with overcommit 2x and AWS launched on-demand fallback; we got 5 on-demand instances for ~3 hours before rollback began. Cost estimate ~ $2k across the outage window. We should update the cost runbook entry for bring-ups.

maya: filed ticket INFRA-3387 to add a guard in the provisioning runner to prevent on-demand fallback for first 30 minutes during new region bring-ups.

sam: rollback finished, but cluster state is inconsistent: kube control-plane VMs created, cloud-provider resources partially deleted. `kubectl get nodes` returns nothing. Need validation steps before reattempt.

leo: propose checklist: 1) confirm subnet tags 2) attach NAT & route table 3) validate IAM roles for node bootstrap 4) quota checks for GPU types 5) dry-run terraform plan with `-target` restrictions 6) controlled canary with 2 nodes.

maya: I'll add that to the nyc bring-up runbook (runbook path: /confluence/infra/region-bringups/nyc) and add a preflight script that checks tags + NAT + quotas.

sam: preflight fails I ran: ```
$ ./preflight.sh --region=us-nyc-1
ERROR: quota check failed: ML.GPU.V100: quota 0, requested 8
ERROR: missing tag: redwood:nodepool on subnet subnet-0a1b2c3d
```

infra-ops: the quota callout is critical — we didn't request GPU quota for nyc. Maya, can you open cloud quota request and mark the ticket with priority-high?

maya: opening request now, ticket CLOUD-9921, ETA 48-72 hours for approval from cloud provider. Marking bring-up blocked until quota is granted.

sam: given the 48-72 hour window, can we pivot to a temporary dedicated pool in nearby region (nyc -> us-east-2) and run validation there? This avoids disrupting teams expecting capacity this week.

leo: yes, we have spare capacity in us-east-2 but networking (latency) for NYC customers increases ~12ms — acceptable for internal testing. Also need to check model locality constraints for private deployments.

maya: will coordinate with product on the temporary region shift. I'll also add a mandatory `--no-on-demand` flag to the provisioning runner to prevent unexpected billing during test bring-ups.

infra-ops: handoff: @anya, can you take ownership for final validation and the handoff doc once quota comes in? Need someone to run the full canary and the health-check script.

anya: taking it. I'll wait for CLOUD-9921 and then run the validation checklist. I'll also capture logs and create a short incident note.

sam: lessons learned to add to runbook: - preflight must fail fast on quota/tags/NAT - provisioning runner needs explicit opt-in for on-demand fallback - add cost alert for >$500 provisioning spend in 1h - require human approval for cross-region redirects

leo: echo on the cost alert. Also add a post-mortem template for bring-ups (short, < 1 page) that includes cost impact and rollback timeline.

maya: updated runbook draft and pushed to /confluence/infra/region-bringups/nyc/drafts. Tagging @sam @leo for review. :eyes:

sam: thanks all. pausing reattempt until quota + tags + NAT verified. I'll post an update in this thread when preflight passes.

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: re-check thread in 72h or when CLOUD-9921 status changes.
